What To Expect
Overview
The Antelope Canyon is known as the photography paradise, where you can see the world's famous light beams. You will have a chance to enter the canyon at noon, which is the prime time to visit Antelope Canyon, to capture the best light.
Explore Antelope Canyon and shoot the most beautiful pictures under the guidance of local Navajo tour guide.
Standing near the steep cliff above Horseshoe Bend, you will enjoy the best scenic view that has a breathtaking 1,000 foot drop.

This tour offers three options for the Antelope Canyon, based on your selection when placing an order.

Upper Antelope Canyon;

Lower Antelope Canyon;

Antelope Canyon X.

The difference between Upper Antelope Canyon and Lower Antelope Canyon:

The Upper Antelope Canyon is completely on the ground, easy for walking. You can observe the light beams radiating from the top of the canyons. The best visiting time is at noon, from 10:00am-2:00pm

Visiting Upper Antelope Canyon requires climbing several staircases up and down. It is much longer and some places are much narrower, difficult for hiking. You can see the dreamlike shapes and curves of rocks under the constantly changing light.

The Lower Antelope Canyon is located several miles from the Upper Antelope Canyon. Prior to the installation of metal stairways, visiting the canyon required climbing pre-installed ladders in certain areas. The lower canyon is in the shape of a "V" and shallower than the Upper Antelope. Lighting is better in the early hours and late morning.

Antelope Canyon X is a slot canyon in Antelope Canyon that is accessible by tour. You will experience a more relaxed atmosphere and smaller groups. This tour consists of 2 slot canyons that you will visit. Our Navajo guides are knowledgeable, ready to help make your trip memorable, whether getting great photos or a great experience.

Horseshoe Bend:

The name was inspired by its unusual shape, a horseshoe-shaped meander of the Colorado River. It is located four miles southwest of Page, AZ, within the Glen Canyon National Recreation Area. Standing near the steep cliff above Horseshoe Bend, you will enjoy the best scenic view that has a breathtaking 1,000 foot drop.

Booking and Confirmation Process
Operator: Mei Tour and Travel
Due to high demand, inventory is mostly synchronous but sometimes not. Our consultant will check real time availability onsite and confirm seats.
You will receive your booking information instantly via email. In the event that you do not receive our email, please check your spam folder, or log into your User Center to check your order status and download your voucher when available.
How To Use
Due to scheduled road closures on the Las Vegas Strip from November 20–22, 2025, and on December 31, 2025, we will be unable to drop guests directly at their hotels in the evenings. Instead, we will drop off at Chinatown Plaza on Spring Mountain Road. Thank you for your understanding.
Your tour guide will contact you before 8pm the day before departure, to double confirm pickup location and time. If you don't receive a call or SMS, please contact us.
No refunds and rescheduld if you are late or unreachable.
Non-refundable Upper Antelope Canyon ticket cannot be cancelled or modified once confirmed.
Horseshoe Bend will be closed from November 3, 2025, to November 6, 2025. During this period, the half-day tours to Antelope Canyon will cancel the Horseshoe Bend stop. The full-day tours to Antelope Canyon will replace the original Horseshoe Bend itinerary with a visit to Glen Canyon Dam.The tour price will remain unchanged during this period.
Upper Antelope Canyon and Lower Antelope Canyon one-day tour, entry time for both is between 11AM and 2PM.
Antelope Canyon is located at the border of Utah and Arizona, which are in different time zones. During the daylight saving time period (from March 9, 2025, to November 2, 2025, with slight variations each year), Utah is one hour ahead of Arizona. When we travel from Utah to Arizona, if the guests' phones do not automatically update the time zone, it may lead them to believe that the entry time to the canyon is incorrect.
During winter time, there is no time difference between Utah and Arizona.
